chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from 'Ali ibn Asbat, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from al-Mu'alla ibn Abi Shihab, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), 'What is the reward for one who visits you?' He (peace be upon him and his family) replied, 'O my son! Whoever visits me while I am alive or after I am dead, or visits your father, or visits your brother, or visits you, it becomes a duty upon me to visit them on the Day of Judgment until I clear them of their sins.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for performing Ziyarah of the Prophet and his family?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the concept of *ziyarah* as a means of spiritual purification, where the Prophet’s personal visitation on the Day of Judgment serves to absolve the visitor of sins. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt, linking physical or spiritual visitation to divine mercy and the removal of spiritual burdens.
